title: Welcome carousel + progressive disclosure for Dedicated capacity setup
creator: Lena Park
description: Design a compact entry experience for teams starting a Dedicated capacity trial that introduces key decisions (capacity sizing, autoscale policy, SLA tier) using a short welcome carousel and progressive disclosure panels. The flow should reduce cognitive load for first-time users by surfacing: a 3-card carousel that explains what Dedicated is, a capacity peek UI that visualizes throughput vs cost, an autoscale policy composer with example presets, and an SLA ribbon showing latency/uptime tradeoffs. Deliverables: high-fidelity screens for the console onboarding modal, a microcopy library for each panel, interactive prototype for user testing, and a small screenshot pack for release notes and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Three-card welcome carousel with L0 copy and illustration (What is Dedicated, How autoscale helps, SLA guarantees) validated in Figma
Capacity peek panel that converts a simple throughput input (rps / concurrent requests) into a visual throughput vs cost chart and a recommended starting capacity with rationale
Autoscale composer with 3 presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) and ability to toggle and preview expected scaling behavior over a 24h simulated traffic curve
SLA ribbon component that shows expected p95 latency and monthly uptime % for selected capacity + autoscale preset
Prototype user-tested with 6 internal engineers or PMs and at least 4 pieces of actionable feedback recorded
Design assets exported (PNG, SVG) and annotated spec added to Confluence with dev handoff checklist
Accessibility review completed: color contrast, keyboard focus states, screen-reader labels for charts
No unresolved blocking dependencies listed in ticket and engineering sign-off on API contract for capacity estimator
comments: 2026-02-26 - Riley Chen (PM): Love the idea of a short carousel. Suggest we keep the initial capacity input to a single number (target rps) to avoid dropdown paralysis. We'll wire the cost assumptions to the billing team later.

2026-03-02 - Sofia Gomez (Staff Eng): Prototype looks great. One note: the capacity estimator needs an API endpoint for a 24h traffic simulation (we currently only have a static estimate endpoint). I'll open an ENG ticket and flag for backend work. Also, charts should be lazy-loaded to avoid initial payload impact.

2026-03-04 - Aisha Khan (Product Designer): Updated illustrations to be single-color line art so they render cleanly in the console's compact header. Added alternate microcopy variants for internationalization (EN/FR).

2026-03-06 - Mateo Alvarez (Design Engineer): Implementability review: autoscale presets map to existing autoscale policy schema except for the new 'burst buffer' field — marked as dependent on ENG-59321. Adjusting acceptance criteria to require fallback when burst buffer is unavailable.
2026-03-09 - Riley Chen (PM): Scheduling a quick moderated usability session on 2026-03-12 with 6 participants (2 infra, 2 PMs, 2 data scientists). Please prepare a script and the prototype link.
2026-03-10 - Sofia Gomez (Staff Eng): ENG-59321 created: capacity-simulator-and-burst-buffer. ETA for API: 2026-03-18. We'll provide a mocked endpoint for prototype testing before API lands.
decisions: Use a 3-card carousel as the primary onboarding entry to keep cognitive load low
Expose only a single numeric input (target RPS) in the first step; advanced tuning behind 'advanced options' progressive disclosure
Autoscale composer will ship with three presets and a toggle to edit thresholds; if 'burst buffer' API is missing, show a disabled control with tooltip explaining server-side limitation
SLA ribbon will be read-only and sourced from the selected capacity tier; include a link to SLA details page for legal language
